lessons.title: No PAN or an Inoperative PAN: Why Your TDS Jumps to 20%

body.text: Your PAN is the address your TDS credit is delivered to. Without one, or with a PAN switched off because it was never linked to Aadhaar, the law deducts at 20% or more and can hold back your refund until you fix it.

children.text: Imran, 31, a freelance graphic designer in Lucknow, invoiced a Delhi agency ₹3,00,000 in tax year 2026-27. He expected 10% TDS, ₹30,000. The agency deducted ₹60,000. His bank did the same to his FD interest, deducting 20% instead of 10%. His PAN was valid, printed on every invoice, and had been for years. The problem was that he had never linked it to his Aadhaar, so the system treated it as if it did not exist.

markDefs.definition: A PAN that has been made inactive, most commonly because it was not linked with Aadhaar by the deadline. For TDS purposes it is treated exactly as if no PAN had been given.

children.text: Section 397(2) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Sections 206AA and 206CC) sets a penalty rate for anyone who receives a payment subject to TDS without furnishing a valid PAN. An invalid or
is treated the same as no PAN at all.

cells: TDS, most payments
The higher of the normal rate or 20%
TDS, a few business payments such as certain purchases of goods and e-commerce sales
The higher of the normal rate or 5%
TCS
The higher of twice the normal rate or 5%, capped at 20% where twice the rate is the higher figure
Payment below the TDS threshold
No TDS at all, PAN or not
Form 121 without a valid PAN
Not valid, so TDS applies

body.title: TDS rate with a valid PAN vs without

children.text: The jump is steepest where normal rates are low. A 1% deduction on a property purchase becomes 20%, twenty times higher. Lottery winnings barely notice, because their normal 30% rate is already above 20%.

body.title: Try It: Imran's Extra TDS
body.prompt: Imran's client paid him ₹3,00,000 in professional fees and his bank credited ₹80,000 of FD interest. Both deducted TDS at 20% because his PAN was inoperative, instead of the normal 10%. How much extra TDS was deducted in total?
body.explanation: On the fees: 20% is ₹60,000 against a normal ₹30,000, an extra ₹30,000. On the interest: 20% is ₹16,000 against ₹8,000, an extra ₹8,000. Together that is ₹38,000 locked up, which he can only recover through his return once his PAN is operative again.

body.title: Quick Check: The Property Deal
body.question: Neeraj is buying a ₹60,00,000 flat in Jaipur. The seller's PAN turns out to be inoperative. At what amount must Neeraj deduct TDS?
options: Nothing, because the seller has no valid PAN
body.explanation: Without a valid PAN, TDS is the higher of the normal 1% and 20%, so ₹12,00,000 instead of ₹60,000. That can derail a sale, which is why buyers and their lawyers now verify the seller's PAN status before signing, and sellers should fix an inoperative PAN before listing a property.

children.text: Why a Valid PAN Becomes Inoperative

Section 262 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 139AA) requires most individuals who hold a PAN and are eligible for Aadhaar to link the two. PANs not linked by the applicable deadline became inoperative.

events.title: General linking deadline
events.description: PANs not linked with Aadhaar by this date became inoperative from 1 July 2023. Linking afterwards requires a fee of ₹1,000.

events.title: CBDT relief for deductors
events.description: Circular 9/2025 said deductors would not be treated as in default for short deduction if the payee's PAN is made operative within two months from the end of the month of payment.

events.title: Deadline for Aadhaar enrolment ID PANs
events.description: People allotted a PAN using an Aadhaar enrolment ID before 1 October 2024 had to intimate their Aadhaar number by this date.

events.title: Those PANs become inoperative
events.description: PANs in that group that were not linked in time were made inoperative.

events.title: New Act
events.description: The linking requirement continues under Section 262 and the higher TDS rate under Section 397(2).

body.title: How the July 2025 relief works for deductors

children.text: Before July 2025, if a deductor paid someone whose PAN was inoperative at the time, the system later raised a short-deduction demand on the deductor, even if the payee linked their PAN a week afterwards. Circular 9/2025 addressed this for deductors.

For payments from 1 April 2024 to 31 July 2025, no higher-rate demand applied if the PAN was made operative by 30 September 2025. For later payments, the relief applies if the PAN becomes operative within two months from the end of the month in which the amount was paid or credited. The circular was issued under the old Act, so check whether equivalent relief has been confirmed for tax year 2026-27 before relying on it.

body.caption: Steps to make your PAN operative again

cells: 1. Check status
On the income tax e-filing portal, use Link Aadhaar Status with your PAN and Aadhaar number
2. Pay the fee
Pay ₹1,000 through e-Pay Tax on the portal (a fee formerly levied under Section 234H)
3. Submit the link request
After the payment reflects, use the Link Aadhaar service. Your name, date of birth and gender must match in both records
4. Wait for activation
The PAN can take up to about 30 days to show as operative again
5. Tell your deductors
Share the updated status with your bank, clients and tenants so future TDS returns to normal rates
6. Recover the excess
Claim the extra TDS already deducted in your return. Refunds are released once the PAN is operative

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Linking Fee
body.textWithBlank: To link Aadhaar with a PAN after the deadline and make it operative again, you must first pay a fee of ₹___.
body.explanation: The fee is ₹1,000, paid through e-Pay Tax on the e-filing portal before the linking request can be submitted. Compared with the extra TDS an inoperative PAN attracts, it is almost always the cheapest fix available.

body.title: Scenario: Imran Fixes It in October
body.scenario: Imran discovers the problem in October 2026, after ₹38,000 of extra TDS has already been deducted. He also has more invoices due to the same agency before March.
body.prompt: What should he do, in what order, and will he get the extra TDS back?
body.modelAnswer: First, check his status on the e-filing portal and confirm the PAN is inoperative because Aadhaar is not linked. Second, pay the ₹1,000 fee through e-Pay Tax and submit the Aadhaar linking request, making sure his name and date of birth match in both records. Third, once the portal shows the PAN as operative, which can take up to about 30 days, email the agency and his bank so they deduct at normal rates on future payments. Fourth, when he files his return for tax year 2026-27, he reports his full income and claims all TDS, including the extra ₹38,000. As long as the credits appear against his PAN, the excess is refunded, though no interest is paid on a refund for the period his PAN stayed inoperative. If he makes the PAN operative quickly after a payment, the deductor may also benefit from CBDT relief, which makes it easier to ask them to cooperate.

body.title: PAN Health Check
steps: Check Link Aadhaar Status on the e-filing portal today, even if you are sure you linked years ago
Confirm your name and date of birth match exactly in PAN and Aadhaar records
Make sure every bank, broker, employer, tenant and client has your current PAN
In Form 26AS or AIS, look for any TDS deducted at 20% and trace why
If you are buying property or paying rent above ₹50,000 a month, verify the other party's PAN status before paying
If a family member is 80 or older or otherwise exempt, keep proof of their exemption handy for banks

body.label: Link Aadhaar Status, e-Filing Portal
body.description: Use the pre-login Link Aadhaar Status and Verify Your PAN services to check whether a PAN is operative, then pay the fee and link if needed.

cards.definition: Higher TDS when a valid PAN is not furnished: the higher of the normal rate or 20% (5% in a few cases). Formerly Sections 206AA and 206CC.
A PAN made inactive, usually for not being linked with Aadhaar. Treated as no PAN for TDS, and refunds are withheld.
Requirement to link PAN with Aadhaar under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Formerly Section 139AA.
₹1,000 payable before linking Aadhaar with PAN after the deadline. Formerly under Section 234H.
July 2025 relief sparing deductors from short-deduction demands if the payee's PAN is made operative within set time limits.
Residents of Assam, Meghalaya and J&K, non-residents, individuals aged 80 or above, and non-citizens.

points: Without a valid PAN, TDS is the higher of the normal rate or 20% under Section 397(2), formerly 206AA
An inoperative PAN, usually one never linked with Aadhaar, is treated exactly as no PAN
The jump is largest on low-rate payments: 1% on a property purchase becomes 20% of the price
An inoperative PAN also means refunds are withheld and no interest is paid for that period, and Form 121 is not valid
The fix is to pay ₹1,000, link Aadhaar under Section 262, wait up to about 30 days, and tell your deductors
Excess TDS already deducted is recovered by claiming it in your return once the PAN is operative
